tool.name: TRACE-5.0
tool.description: Dynamic molecular surveillance of viral transmission networks
tool.command: ln -s '$fasta' input.fasta && #if $dates.kind == "file": ## trace50 detects TSV by file extension, so the symlink must ## carry the real extension for metadata parsing to work. ln -s '$dates.meta' meta.$dates.meta.ext && #end if trace50 --fasta input.fasta --out-dir results #if $dates.kind == "file": --meta meta.$dates.meta.ext #if $dates.id_col: --id-col '$dates.id_col' #end if #if $dates.date_col: --date-col '$dates.date_col' #end if #end if #if $distances: --distances '$distances' #end if $adv.use_robust $adv.info_danno #if $adv.seq_len: --seq-len $adv.seq_len #end if --mu $adv.mu --tau-bar $adv.tau_bar --omega $adv.omega --fdr $adv.fdr --alpha-adequacy $adv.alpha_adequacy --max-delta-t $adv.max_delta_t --threshold $adv.threshold --r0 $adv.r0 --min-size $adv.min_size --max-depth $adv.max_depth --tn93-ambig '$adv.tn93_ambig'

param.label: Input alignment
param.help: Aligned nucleotide FASTA. Sampling dates are read from headers (e.g. name|2015.5) unless a metadata file is supplied below.

param.name: kind
param.label: Sampling dates source
param.help: Dates drive the temporal deconvolution; they can come from FASTA headers or a separate metadata table.

param.label: Metadata file
param.help: CSV or TSV with a taxon-ID column and a collection-date column. Decimal years, ISO dates, and other common date strings are parsed positionally.

param.label: Taxon ID column
param.help: Metadata column matching the FASTA headers

param.label: Date column
param.help: Metadata column holding collection dates

param.label: Precomputed distance matrix (optional)
param.help: tn93 -t 1.0 output: a header line then ID1,ID2,Distance rows with IDs matching the FASTA headers. When supplied, internal TN93 computation is skipped.

param.label: Substitution rate (mu)
param.help: Retroviral substitution rate in substitutions per site per year

param.label: Intra-host coalescent depth (tau-bar)
param.help: Mean intra-host coalescent depth in years

param.label: Surveillance delay (omega)
param.help: Clinical surveillance delay timescale in years

param.label: FDR threshold
param.help: Bayesian FDR threshold for supported acute transmission dyads

param.label: Clock-adequacy alpha
param.help: Significance threshold for the molecular clock adequacy test; dyads failing it receive Bayes factor zero

param.label: Max sampling separation
param.help: Maximum sampling-time separation between dyad members, in years

param.label: Static distance threshold
param.help: Static genetic-distance cutoff used for the comparison benchmark network (e.g. 0.015 = 1.5% TN93)

param.label: Basic reproductive ratio (R0)
param.help: R0 used within the transmission-network branching model

param.label: Minimum community size
param.help: Minimum leaf community size for STEVE spectral deconvolution

param.label: Max AutoClock depth
param.help: Maximum recursion depth for the AutoClock root-to-tip engine

param.label: Robust Bayes factors
param.help: Use min-max robust Bayes factors over the biological uncertainty domain

param.label: InfoDANNO
param.help: Use site-specific information-theoretic transmission odds instead of aggregate distances

param.label: Sequence length override
param.help: Alignment length L used by DANNO (k = d * L). Defaults to the median non-gap sequence length.

param.label: TN93 ambiguity handling
param.help: Ambiguity handling for internal TN93 distances, as tn93 -a: resolve, average, skip, gapmm, or a list of ambiguity codes to resolve. Ignored when a distance matrix is supplied.

tool.help:
TRACE-5.0: Dynamic Molecular Surveillance of Viral Transmission Networks =========================================================================
**What question does this method answer?**
Which sequence pairs in a dated alignment represent plausible direct or recent transmission events, how do they resolve into communities with estimated clock velocities and TMRCAs, and what do the networks imply about the size of the actively transmitting population?
**How it works**
TRACE-5.0 screens candidate transmission dyads using TN93 distances computed internally (or a user-supplied distance matrix), then scores each dyad under DANNO — a Bayes-factor calibration of genetic distance against sampling-time separation under a physical molecular clock. Dyads failing the clock-adequacy test are purged, and surviving edges are controlled at a Bayesian false discovery rate. STEVE spectral deconvolution resolves communities and AutoClock estimates their clock velocities and TMRCAs; CHIN infers macro-scale quantities such as the active transmitting pool and surveillance sampling fraction.
**Inputs**
- An aligned nucleotide FASTA file. Sampling dates are parsed from sequence headers (e.g. ``name|2015.5``) unless a metadata CSV/TSV with taxon IDs and dates is supplied. - Optionally, a precomputed ``tn93 -t 1.0`` distance CSV to bypass the internal distance computation.
**Outputs**
- **Visualization dossier (JSON)**: the full result, including KPIs, edges, nodes, communities, and macro-scaling estimates - **Acute transmission dyads (CSV)**: one row per screened dyad with distance, time separation, Bayes factor, PEP, q-value, clock-adequacy p-value, and support status - **AutoClock communities (CSV)**: per-community size, clock velocity, TMRCA with confidence interval, and operational tier - **Patient surveillance assignments (CSV)**: per-taxon degrees in the static and supported networks, cluster and community memberships
